# Diagnostic codes

<!-- Generated by scripts/diagnostics-doc.mjs. Edit packages/core/src/diagnostics.ts. -->

Every diagnostic Speculoos emits carries a stable `code`. Codes are a public
contract: they end up in CI configuration through `speculoos lint --allow`, so
renaming one breaks somebody's build.

25 codes in total — 13 error, 9 warning, 3 info.

```sh
speculoos lint spec.yaml --allow NOT,IF --max-severity error
```

`lint` exits non-zero when any diagnostic at or above `--max-severity`
(default `warning`) survives the allow-list. An `--allow` entry that is not a
known code is reported as a warning rather than silently ignored.

| Code | Severity | Emitted by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BAD_DOCUMENT_NAME` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | A document name is unusable. Names end up in every TypeId and therefore in every URL, so they must be stable and caller-supplied rather than derived from a filesystem path. |
| `DOCUMENT_EMPTY` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | The file parsed to nothing. Usually an empty file or one that is all comments. |
| `DOCUMENT_UNREADABLE` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | The file could not be read. Check the path and permissions. |
| `INVALID_SCHEMA` | error | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | A schema position holds something that is neither an object nor a boolean. |
| `NO_BASE_PATH` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | A relative $ref was found with no base path to resolve it against. |
| `PARSE_ERROR` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | The file is not valid YAML or JSON. |
| `REF_CYCLE` | error | `@speculoos/adapter-kit` | A $ref chain closes on itself with nothing in between. A self-referential *type* is fine; this is a ref pointing at a ref pointing back. |
| `REMOTE_REF_DISABLED` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | A $ref points at a URL and remote loading is off, which is the default. Fetching whatever a spec names at build time is a supply-chain decision, so it is opt-in rather than automatic. |
| `REMOTE_REF_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `@speculoos/loader` | A $ref points at a URL and remote loading is not implemented. Vendor the document instead. |
| `UNKNOWN_ACTION` | error | `@speculoos/asyncapi` | An AsyncAPI 3.x operation declares an action other than "send" or "receive". |
| `UNKNOWN_DIALECT` | error | `@speculoos/cli` | A document declares neither `openapi` nor `asyncapi`. Swagger 2.0 is recognised and refused by name — convert it first. |
| `UNRESOLVED_CHANNEL` | error | `@speculoos/asyncapi` | An operation names a channel that the document does not define. |
| `UNRESOLVED_REF` | error | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | A $ref names something that is not in the project. The field still renders, marked as an unresolved reference, rather than vanishing. |
| `ALLOF_CONFLICT` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | Two allOf branches cannot be merged — most often a union intersected with a scalar. The first member is kept. Nothing is guessed, which is why this is a diagnostic and not a silent choice. |
| `DEPENDENT_SCHEMAS` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `DYNAMIC_REF` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `HIDDEN_TYPE_REFERENCED` | warning | `@speculoos/transforms` | A type was hidden but something still links to it, so a renderer will show a broken link. Usually means the predicate was too narrow. |
| `IF` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `NOT` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `SCHEMA_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED` | warning | `@speculoos/asyncapi` | A message declares a schemaFormat that is not JSON Schema — Avro, Protobuf, OpenAPI-flavoured. The message still appears; its payload shape does not. |
| `UNEVALUATED_ITEMS` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `UNEVALUATED_PROPERTIES` | warning | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | The keyword constrains validation in a way that has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders. |
| `ALLOF_UNMERGED` | info | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | An allOf branch was kept as an intersection rather than flattened into its siblings. |
| `NO_DIALECT` | info | `@speculoos/loader` | A document declares no $schema. The default dialect is assumed; say so explicitly if that is wrong. |
| `UNION_WITH_SIBLINGS` | info | `@speculoos/jsonschema` | oneOf or anyOf sits alongside other keywords. Both apply, so the result is an intersection of the union with its siblings. The common required-only-branches idiom folds into a note instead. |

## Unsupported keywords

Six of the codes above are generated from a JSON Schema keyword rather than
written out. `lower` strips a leading `$` and converts camelCase to
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, so `if` becomes `IF` and `$dynamicRef` becomes
`DYNAMIC_REF`.

They all mean the same thing: the keyword constrains *validation* in a way that
has no display form. The node renders as `unsupported` with the reason
attached, and whatever else the schema said still renders — a field is never
dropped silently.

## Reading them in code

```ts
import { DIAGNOSTIC_CODES, describeDiagnostic } from "@speculoos/core";

describeDiagnostic("ALLOF_CONFLICT")?.severity; // "warning"
```
